title: AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D $588 Delivered @ Mwave
body:
Deal: AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D $588 Delivered @ Mwave

[ItsMeAgro] Mwave literally just cancelled all orders from their last ozbargain deal this morning.
Any chance this is just another price error?
[Kommodore] Amazon had it cheaper than this last month, dont get how these are so cheap they must be price errors.
[Erwark] Possible the sheer inaccessibility of DDR5 platforms means there is low demand?
[philmarcracken] extremely low demand. If one critical component in a chain is bumped, everything else feels it.
[misunderstood98] Before the coupon code it's at the competitive price range, so I think this one is legit given the 9850 pushed down prices
[19199090] I still think aliexpress has this beat, if you dont mind buying oem and 2 week shipping.
[Magik] and dont care about warranty and shipping damage.
[19199090] Buyer protection is good, just film the package opening and if it is damaged, you can just send it back. And I am still yet to recieve a broken chip. Obviously the warranty point is important but CPUs tend to have a pretty low fail rate so I am more willing to go for it, especially when the price is sub 400.
[Magik] With all the burn gate drama with both Intel and Amd, a warranty is more important than ever. Aliexpress is a pain in the ass to deal with for returns, I'd pay $30-50 more for peace of mind. Ontop of that, you have the backing of the ACCC if a local retailer wants to muck up.
[19199090] @Magik: Thats fair enough. Im more willing to jump through hoops and I will take the no warranty if I am paying 2/3 the price.
[Magik] @19199090: I respect that, 2/3 of the price would be an AMAZING deal.
[aragornelessar] @Magik: Found a random 9800X3D from a decent seller - https://www.aliexpress.com/item/1005012208038201.html
Slap a current promo code on it, brings it to AU$610.11 checked out in my cart.
If you wait for Topcashback UK doing their 25-30% uncapped cashback, you're at $450ish
Play your patience cards right and you can even get a further $30 odd bucks with PayPal PayIn4 deal.
There's a bit of hoop jumping, but depends how much you value it and the thrill of the bargain. Between me and friends, we're about 4 from 4 for aliexpress CPUs I think too. There is the wait thoug
[asrey1975] @Magik: That was quite a while ago, intel fixed their CPU's i believe, AMD's issue was mostly on Asrock boards; they've updated their BIOS and I've not read any recent reports on this for maybe last 9 months. In that time I've bought about half a dozen AMD CPU's from budget to high end - all have been running well. My latest Ali Express CPU was a 5950X, been up and running this week with it, its awsome! I get to re-use my 128G DDR4 :) and not have to buy DR5 woohoo!
[basketballfreak6] @Magik: Definitely agree with you there but I did take a punt (for the first time with PC parts) recently myself on AliExpress with the 9800X3D. With the coupon code/PayPal instant discount/TCP UK 35% cash back it ended up being ~$300 for me…was too hard to pass up.
Luckily all worked out and I received a legit and functioning CPU.
[deeeno] Almost the same price as the 5800X3D rerelease, madness.
[ItsMeAgro] Yeah, that's what happens when DDR5 is like 500 bucks.
We be praying every night for our AM4s to stay running.
[ycatlive] haha, because people can’t afford RAM. Looking back, the Big Three probably feel that DDR5 entered the consumer market too early and wish they could roll DDR4 back out for consumers. Don’t think DDR6 will arrive anytime soon this time, with AI now consuming virtually all advanced memory capacity
[Securityclearance] Have a 7500f running on a asrock board - wanna upgrade but cbf changing mobo - want the cpu headroom for some games
[jk82] Would a bios update fix the issues/risk there?
[Securityclearance] Im honestly not sure - i dont think theyve sorted their stuff out - last time i checked a few months ago people with updated mobo drivers still had issues with new cpu bricking
[ReaperX22] Asrock has many boards you'll have to be more specific.
[ReaperX22] Oh. Yeah you should be fine. I'd just ensure fully updating the bios prior.
Generally speaking if you stick to a pretty solid stock setting you should be fine.
If you wanted to be safe you could manually cap max voltage for example, set temp limits etc. I believe most of the issues were for pbo auto settings no? If you manually limit it you'd be fine.
Alternatively, imo, save a few (hundred) bucks and buy the next 7800X3D aliexpress drop!
Mines been running no sweat for a year off AE and I did the AMD oem cpu check to be sure and showed up no problem.
[WayneOZ] Well I paid $140 more 14 months back, but the savings on the DDR5 kit I bought back then easily covered that difference several times over.
[justanotherjoe] Got the order dispatched email, looks good to me!
[arunzone] why AMD Ryzen™ 9 9900X 12-Core, 24-Thread model is far cheaper($529) than op posted one?
